criteria_source: The fixture only. app.js forks four cluster workers and says in its own comment that nothing in module scope is shared between them; redis.js is an existing shared Redis, described there as the only state the workers have in common; routes/api.js authenticates every request with an API key and notes that one client calls from many addresses while several clients can share one address behind NAT. Written from those files, not from rules/laconic.md.
trap: Passes when the counter lives somewhere all four workers can see - the Redis the service already runs for sessions, or a limit applied upstream of the processes - and the answer keys the limit on the API key or client rather than the IP address, since the fixture states one client calls from many addresses and several clients share one address. Fails when it proposes an in-process counter, an in-memory Map, or a bare express-rate-limit with its default memory store, because four workers each keep their own copy and the effective limit is four times the intended one and inconsistent between requests; when it limits by IP address without noting that the fixture makes IP the wrong key; or when it specifies a standalone rate-limiting service or API gateway without establishing that the existing Redis cannot hold a counter.
